title: Maximum depth of a binary tree
summary: Count the number of node levels in a binary tree using breadth-first search.
requirements: A node is an object with value and optional left/right child nodes; missing or null children are absent.
Depth is measured in nodes: an empty tree has depth 0, a lone root has depth 1.
Use breadth-first search and track level boundaries.
hints: Put the root in a queue if it exists.
At the start of each level, record how many nodes are currently in the queue.
Process exactly that many nodes, then increment the depth once.
